narrative:
The model predicts you have a 15% chance of failing your final year, which is low but enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your past academic record, your ambitions for higher education, and your weekend social habits. Surprisingly, the strongest factor actually worked in your favor: having no previous class failures is a very positive signal compared to many students who passed. Your clear desire to pursue higher education also pushed the prediction toward passing. However, your pattern of going out with friends on weekends had the opposite effect. While many students who succeed report very low weekend alcohol consumption and moderate social outings, your higher level of going out appears to have pulled the prediction toward failure, outweighing the protective effects of your clean record and strong ambitions.

To improve, consider whether your weekend social life is quietly affecting your study consistency or energy levels during the week. Even with no past failures and clear goals for university, tightening your focus during term time could raise your chances further and potentially remove the need for remedial classes.
